q: 1. Security deposit deducted at 5% from contractor's bills is
options: refunded when the contractor has completed the work
refunded even before the completion of the work provided good progress has been established
retained till the expected life of the structure of say 100 years and spent for maintenance
refunded when the defect liability period of six months or one monsoon whichever is later is over
explain: The deposit is released only after the defect liability period ends.

q: 2. Which of the following documents should be prepared and submitted by a contractor?
explain: The bid document is prepared and submitted by the contractor in response to a tender notice.

q: 3. Direct purchase can be done for construction work when the amount is
explain: Per public procurement regulations, direct purchase (without formal bidding) is permitted for works valued up to Rs. 0.3 million.

q: 4. The pre-tender stage of construction requires
explain: All of these are done before tendering.

q: 5. The pre-tender stage of construction requires:
explain: The pre-tender stage involves site selection, land acquisition, and design finalization - all necessary before floating the tender.

q: 6. According to "Contract Act 2055" the number of classes of contractor are
explain: The Nepal Contract Act/Public Procurement regulations categorize contractors into four classes: A, B, C, and D.

q: 7. While filling the tender for any work, the contractor considers quotation?
explain: A contractor must evaluate the site conditions, labor market, and technical requirements (specifications) to provide an accurate and competitive price.

q:
8. Tender is called for
i) to minimize the cost of an item
ii) to find exact rate of item of unknown item
iii) to take minimum rate from contractor
explain: Tenders invite open competition to minimize work costs and obtain competitive rates from contractors[cite: 1].

q: 9. Which of the following information is generally not published in a tender notice?
explain: Performance bond requirements are typically specified in the contract document rather than published details in the initial tender notice.

q: 10. Site order book is used for recording
options: indents for materials to be ordered
explain: It records the engineer's instructions to the contractor.

q: 11. By using the method of sealed quotation, which of the following cannot procured?
options: all of the above can be procured
explain: The sealed quotation method can be used for procurement of works, goods, and services alike - so all of the above can be procured.

q: 12. If damage occurred within specified time internal, it falls on the work of
explain: During the construction and defects liability period, the contractor is responsible for damage to the works.

q: 13. The estimated cost of works must be quoted in the tender notice for works worth up to
explain: Per the answer key, up to 2 crore.

q: 14. The authority of Gazetted third officer for the approval of estimate is (Source:PPR 2064(14))
explain: Financial delegation under Nepalese PPR authorizes Gazetted 3rd class officers up to NRs 10 million[cite: 1].

q: 15. The price of tender document for the bidding amount upto two crore is (Source:PPR2064(48))
explain: According to Nepal's PPR, tender documents for projects up to 20 million (2 crore) cost 3,000 NRS.

q: 16. The first step for formulation of any contract is
explain: Contract formulation begins with inviting bids from the public or pre-qualified vendors through publishing the tender notice.

q: 17. The amount of money deposited while bidding a tender as a guarantee of the party's willingness of carry out the work is called
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) or bid security is deposited along with the bid submission to prove the bidder's genuine intent to undertake the work.

q: 18. Amount required to be deposited by contractor while submitting tender is
explain: Earnest money is the amount a contractor deposits along with the tender submission as a guarantee of serious intent.

q: 19. The price adjustment clause is essential for contract having duration greater than ……… months.
explain: Per the answer key, 12 months.

q: 20. *Acquisition of land for any construction should be performed :
explain: The owner must have possession of the land before inviting contractors to bid to avoid delays and legal issues.

q: 21. Which of the following is the ultimate method of dispute resolution in any contract
explain: Court litigation is the last resort.

q: 22. As per the financial regulation minimum time required for tender notice is for NCB contract:
explain: Financial regulations stipulate a minimum of 30 days for tender notice period for National Competitive Bidding (NCB) contracts.

q: 23. The bid review committee consists of ……… members of persons.
explain: Per the answer key, 3.

q: 24. The penalty provision in any contract agreement is
explain: Per the answer key, 0.05% per day.

q: 25. The minimum number of consulting firms for direct purchase of service is
explain: Per the answer key, 3.

q: 26. Relation between contractor, consultant & engineer should be
options: should not create the stage of quarreling
if any problem created, there should be mutualization for discussion
explain: Professional harmony and collaborative problem-solving between all parties are essential for project success.

q: 27. Contractor's prequalification is required for project cost above (Source: PPR2064(3))
explain: Under Public Procurement Regulations (PPR 2064, Rule 3), mandatory pre-qualification is specified for large projects exceeding threshold values.

q: 28. The railway projects are treated as
explain: Railway construction involves massive earthworks and heavy infrastructure, placing it in the heavy construction category.

q: 29. An offer in writing to execute some specified civil works at certain rates within a fixed time under certaion conditions of contract is called:
explain: A bid (or tender submission) is a formal written offer submitted by a contractor detailing terms, rates, and timeframe to perform specified work.

q: 30. Which of the following column is left blank in Bidding documentary by the employing agency?
explain: In Bill of Quantities (BOQ) tender documents, the employer supplies descriptions, units, and estimated quantities while leaving the unit rates blank for bidders to quote.

q: 31. The document announcing to prospective bidders that the owner is ready to receive the bids is called:
explain: An Invitation for Bids (IFB) or Notice to Bidders publicly notifies qualified contractors that an employer is accepting bids for a project.

q: 32. The supplementary specification prepared and applied if the standard specification does not cover the requirement of works under a contract is called:
explain: The answer key indicates 'performance specification', though in many contexts, these are also referred to as 'special specifications'.

q: 33. A contractor's role in construction includes:
explain: Maintaining safety at the construction site is a core responsibility of the contractor, unlike payment/certification which are the client/engineer's roles.

q: 34. Which of the followings should be practiced first if a dispute arises in a contract?
explain: Amicable settlement (direct negotiation between parties) is typically the first step attempted before escalating to mediation, adjudication, or arbitration.

q: 35. The document giving the information about the tender, prequalification, contractor, construction, procurement of materials and services is called
explain: The tender document (or bid document) contains all the necessary information for a contractor to prepare a bid.

q: 36. Time extension may need to be granted due to
explain: Time extensions can be warranted by force majeure events as well as delays caused by the purchaser/employer - both a and b.

q: 37. The purpose of bid evaluation is to evaluate
explain: Evaluation identifies the lowest evaluated substantially responsive bidder.

q: 38. While filling the tender for any work, the contractor considers
explain: A contractor considers site conditions, material availability, and labour availability while preparing a tender bid - all of the above.

q: 39. The remuneration of dispute adjudication board is paid by
explain: The client and contractor share the cost.

q: 40. When actual cost of construction plus certain profit is paid to the contractor then such a contract is known as
explain: A cost-plus-percentage contract pays the contractor actual costs incurred plus an agreed percentage as profit.
